story_type: pad abort test, escape tower pulls capsule off the pad
hook: No rocket under it. Just a capsule and an escape tower.
narration: This capsule blasted off a launch pad with no rocket under it.
May sixth, twenty ten, White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico. NASA was testing the escape system for its Orion capsule.
If a rocket fails on the pad, the tower of motors on top has to drag the crew away before the blast can reach them.
So NASA lit it on purpose. The capsule hit about four hundred forty five miles an hour in the first three seconds.
It climbed to about one point two miles high, then the parachutes came out.
Three main chutes opened over the desert.
outcome: The capsule touched down at about sixteen miles an hour, roughly a mile from the pad, in a test NASA called a success.

location_card.place: White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico

title: Capsule yanked off the pad at 445 mph
description:
On May 6, 2010, NASA flew the Pad Abort-1 test at White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico: Orion's launch abort system pulled a test capsule off the pad and it parachuted down about a mile away.

Footage: NASA Johnson Space Center video, via Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Orion_Pad_Abort-1_Launch_Abort_System_Flight_Test.webm
